info.desc: Bleach is the debut album by the American grunge band Nirvana. It was released on June 15, 1989 through the independent record label Sub Pop. Bleach originally sold a mere 30,000 copies, but following the enormous success of the band's second album, Nevermind (1991), fans discovered Nirvana's obscure debut. It has since been certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America, making it one of only two albums released on Sub Pop to have received platinum certification. The main sessions for Bleach took place at Reciprocal Recording Studios in Seattle, Washington, with local producer Jack Endino manning the board. .

podcast.body: Nirvana's first album for Subpop, "Bleach," was recorded in June 1990. The total cost to produce the album was a mere $606.17, showcasing the band's humble beginnings. "In June of 1990, they recorded Bleach, their first album for Subpop. Total cost to make $606.17."

podcast.body: Recorded in 1988 for a total cost of $606.17. Kurt Cobain didn't have the money, so his friend Jason Everman, a commercial fisherman from Alaska, paid the bill. As a thank-you, Everman was credited in the liner notes as having played guitar, even though he played no notes on the recording. "Kurt made it look like Jason played on the record, but let's be clear, he did not."

podcast.body: The band's debut record, released on June 15, 1989, by the "perpetually broke" Sub Pop Records out of Seattle. Only 1,000 copies of the original vinyl version were pressed on white vinyl. A mint condition copy of this initial pressing can fetch as much as $5,500 today. "On June 15, 1989, the first Nirvana record came out. It was called Bleach."

podcast.body: The recording fee for Nirvana's debut album *Bleach* was $606.17, which was paid to Jack Endino at Reciprocal Recording by Jason Everman. Everman, who briefly served as Nirvana's second guitarist, was given fake credit on the album for his financial generosity, although he did not play on the record. "He never played on the album, but was given fake credit on the record for his financial generosity."

podcast.body: This was Nirvana's debut album. The band had planned a follow-up, tentatively titled *Sheep*, to be released while they were still with Sub Pop. "There was supposed to be a record between Bleach and Never Mind, or more accurately, the record after Bleach was originally envisioned as an album entitled Sheep."
